questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked

Tests ability to implement a small, production-like service with proper isolation, boot-time persistence, and operational hygiene on a RHCSA beginner level. It covers non-root execution, basic HTTP serving, log management, firewall exposure, and a simple verification plan.

## Key Concepts

- systemd service basics (User, WorkingDirectory, ExecStart, Restart)
- non-root process isolation
- stdout/stderr redirection to a log file and log rotation
- logrotate configuration
- firewalld port exposure
- basic health check with curl

## Code Example

```bash
# systemd unit (webserver.service)
[Unit]
Description=Simple static web server

[Service]
User=webuser
Group=webuser
WorkingDirectory=/var/www/html
ExecStart=/bin/sh -c '/usr/bin/python3 -m http.server 8080 --bind 0.0.0.0 > /var/log/webserver.log 2>&1'
Restart=on-failure

[Install]
WantedBy=multi-user.target
```

```ini
# logrotate (cron-like daily rotation)
 /var/log/webserver.log {
   daily
   rotate 7
   copytruncate
   missingok
   notifempty
   create 0640 webuser webuser
 }
```

## Follow-up Questions

- How would you add TLS termination for the same setup behind a reverse proxy?
- What changes would you make to support multiple concurrent pages or a small SPA?

```bash
}
```

## Why This Is Asked
Tests hands-on SSH hardening in RHCSA-style tasks, ensuring secure key-based authentication, proper file permissions, and correct access controls.

- SSH daemon hardening (sshd_config)

## Code Example

```bash
# as root or user with sudo
mkdir -p /home/deploy/.ssh
chmod 700 /home/deploy/.ssh
ssh-keygen -t rsa -b 4096 -f /home/deploy/.ssh/id_rsa -N '' -C 'deploy@host'
cat /home/deploy/.ssh/id_rsa.pub >> /home/deploy/.ssh/authorized_keys

```

## Why This Is Asked
Tests systemd mastery: timers, dependencies, failure handling, and idempotent logging.

## Key Concepts
- systemd timer and service wiring
- network-online.target dependency
- OnFailure retry flow
- centralized log rotation for backup logs

## Code Example
```ini
# /etc/systemd/system/backup.service
[Unit]
Description=Nightly backup
After=network-online.target
Wants=network-online.target

[Service]
Type=oneshot
ExecStart=/usr/local/bin/daily-backup.sh
StandardOutput=append:/var/log/backup.log
StandardError=append:/var/log/backup.log
```
```ini
# /etc/systemd/system/backup.timer
[Unit]
Description=Daily backup timer

[Timer]
OnCalendar=daily 02:00
Persistent=true
Unit=backup.service

[Install]
WantedBy=timers.target
```
```ini
# /etc/systemd/system/backup.service.d/override.conf
[Unit]
OnFailure=backup-retry.service
```
```ini
# /etc/systemd/system/backup-retry.service
[Unit]
Description=Retry backup after failure
After=network-online.target

[Service]
Type=oneshot
ExecStart=/bin/bash -lc 'sleep 900; /usr/local/bin/daily-backup.sh'
```
```ini
# /etc/logrotate.d/backup
/var/log/backup.log {
  daily
  rotate 7
  compress
  missingok
  notifempty
}
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you add a health check to prevent overlap with a running backup?
- How would you audit and alert on failures?

## Why This Is Asked
Tests ability to design automated, safe backups with removable media, SELinux considerations, and systemd workflow. It exercises device detection, label relabeling, incremental rsync, and retention.

## Key Concepts
- Auto-detection and mounting of USB drives
- SELinux labeling on external media
- Incremental backups with rsync and --link-dest
- Daily date-based backup directories and retention
- Systemd path/unit/timer integration

## Code Example
```javascript
// usb-backup.sh (example content)
#!/bin/bash
set -e
SRC="/srv/app"
ROOT="/mnt/usb-backup/backups"
TODAY=$(date +%Y%m%d)
YESTERDAY=$(date -d yesterday +%Y%m%d)
DST="$ROOT/$TODAY"
mkdir -p "$DST"
rsync -a --link-dest="$ROOT/$YESTERDAY" "$SRC/" "$DST/"
restorecon -R "$DST"
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you test failure scenarios (drive removal during backup)?
- How would you scale to multiple USB drives and ensure single-source of truth for backups?

```javascript
# /etc/rsyslog.d/60-forward.conf (illustrative)
$DefaultNetstreamDriver gtls
$ActionSendStreamDriver gtls
$TLSCACertificateFile /etc/pki/tls/certs/ca-bundle.crt

$TLSKeyFile /etc/pki/tls/private/rsyslog-client.key

$ActionQueueFileName fwdq1
$ActionQueueMaxDiskSpace 1g

$ActionQueueTimeoutEnqueue 86400
$ActionQueueSaveOnShutdown on

# Forward all application logs
*.* @@loghub.example.com:10514
```

